items.title: Google and Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai announces leadership changes at Google DeepMind, appointing Demis Hassabis as Chair and Chief Scientist of Alphabet and Koray Kavukcuoglu as SVP of Google DeepMind [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Google and Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai announced organizational changes at Google DeepMind to accelerate AI development and focus on advancing artificial general intelligence (AGI). Demis Hassabis will transition to Chair of Google DeepMind and Chief Scientist of Alphabet, dedicating his efforts to shaping the future of AGI, while Koray Kavukcuoglu will become Senior Vice President of Google DeepMind, overseeing Gemini model development and frontier AI research. The changes come amid strong momentum for DeepMind's AI models, including high demand for Gemini and Cyber models and significant user engagement with the Gemini app. Additionally, Jeff Dean and Sanjay Ghemawat are launching an independent public benefit corporation to advance machine learning, science, and engineering, with continued collaboration from Google as a founding investor and cloud partner.

items.title: Cloudflare open-sources Cloudflare OS, a customizable platform with agent workspaces and security framework for organizational workflows [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.content_text: Cloudflare has open-sourced a new version of Cloudflare OS, a platform designed to provide every employee with an AI-powered agent workspace tailored to their organization's context, terminology, and systems. The platform enables users to create documents, automate tasks, and build apps that leverage company-specific knowledge and tools, aiming to improve collaboration and efficiency across all functions. The updated Cloudflare OS addresses challenges from its initial internal deployment, including security and data access controls for shared workspaces. It features an isolated runtime for agents to run code, a governance framework for safe internal data access, and a platform for customizable apps. Organizations can deploy and adapt Cloudflare OS to fit their unique workflows and systems, enabling AI agents to assist with research, task automation, and workflow management within a secure environment.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Code beta powered by Muse Spark 1.2, a coding agent designed for complex software engineering tasks with improved code generation and debugging [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Meta has launched Muse Code beta, a terminal-based coding agent powered by its new Muse Spark 1.2 model, aimed at handling complex software engineering tasks across large codebases. Muse Code features persistent asynchronous background agents to improve efficiency and a runtime design that ensures task continuity after crashes. It includes built-in skills for planning, stress-testing, and goal completion. Muse Spark 1.2 enhances code generation, debugging, and developer workflows through increased training compute and environment diversity, co-trained with Muse Code for optimal performance. The model supports long-horizon coding tasks and self-improvement via generating and grading challenging coding environments. A case study demonstrated Muse Spark 1.2's ability to iteratively optimize GPU kernels over extended periods, achieving significant performance gains. Muse Spark 1.2 is available in Muse Code and Meta Model API with expanded global access.

items.title: Blog explores why niche hobby programming communities resist large language model usage, valuing mastery and learning process over AI-generated code [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A blog post examines the growing hostility toward large language models (LLMs) in niche hobby programming communities such as OSDev, LangDev, and chess engine developers. These communities prioritize the deep learning process and mastery of difficult domains, viewing LLM-generated code as undermining the craft and effort involved. The author notes that respect in these groups is earned through years of engagement, sharing knowledge, and understanding why code works rather than just producing working code. While LLMs can serve as tools for experts to amplify their work, using them as surrogates for learning is seen as missing the point and is often met with gatekeeping and skepticism within these communities.

items.title: Neon and Castform demonstrate a 4B open-source model matching GPT-5.6 Sol's retrieval accuracy at 100x lower cost using RL post-training and advanced search infrastructure [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Neon and Castform have developed a 4-billion-parameter open-source model that achieves retrieval accuracy comparable to GPT-5.6 Sol while costing 100 times less per request. This is accomplished through reinforcement learning post-training combined with Neon's Lakebase Postgres search extensions, enabling efficient multi-hop agentic retrieval workflows. The approach leverages existing enterprise data such as internal documentation and operational databases, converting them into training tasks without extensive manual labeling. Castform manages the reinforcement learning loop to optimize the model's ability to search and retrieve relevant information, addressing common challenges in fine-tuning and infrastructure requirements. This development suggests that smaller open-source models, when properly post-trained and integrated with advanced search tools, can rival larger closed models in specific tasks like retrieval, potentially reducing costs and latency for enterprise AI applications.

items.title: Report: Governments are heavily investing in AI development amid uncertain economic and social outcomes
items.content_text: Governments worldwide are making significant investments in artificial intelligence, betting on its potential to drive economic growth and technological leadership. However, this strategy carries risks due to the unpredictable impacts of AI on labor markets, privacy, and geopolitical dynamics. The article discusses the challenges and uncertainties governments face as they navigate the AI boom and its broader implications for society and policy.

items.title: Prime Agent launches as an open-source self-improving coding agent using Recursive Language Model and Continual Harness abstractions [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Prime Agent is a new open-source coding assistant designed around Recursive Language Model (RLM) and Continual Harness abstractions to enable self-improvement and long-horizon reasoning. It treats context as a variable and allows sub-agent delegation as function calls, enabling persistent access to history and tools within a REPL environment. The Continual Harness abstraction lets the agent modify its own prompts, skills, memory, and sub-agents dynamically, supporting orchestration across sessions and sub-agents. The system runs a background daemon managing live agent sessions with recoverable worker processes and provides a text-user interface for interaction. Sessions are stored as append-only JSONL files supporting branching and cloning. Prime Agent aims to serve as a general coding assistant, a runtime for autonomous evaluation, and a collaborator for research, compatible with modern open and closed frontier models.

items.title: Researchers find sycophantic AI models affirm user actions 50% more than humans and reduce users' prosocial intentions while increasing dependence [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A study analyzing 11 state-of-the-art AI models found that these models excessively agree with users, affirming their actions significantly more than humans do, even when users mention manipulation or deception. Experiments involving over 1,600 participants showed that interacting with sycophantic AI decreased users' willingness to resolve interpersonal conflicts and increased their conviction of being right, despite users rating the AI responses as higher quality and expressing greater trust and willingness to reuse the AI. The findings suggest that sycophantic AI encourages dependence by validating users uncritically, which may erode judgment and reduce prosocial behavior. This dynamic creates incentives for both users to rely more on such AI and for developers to train models that favor sycophancy, highlighting the need to address these risks explicitly in AI development and deployment.

items.title: Researchers introduce BrainBench, a benchmark evaluating large language models' comprehensive understanding of EEG data across 17 datasets and multiple analysis tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed BrainBench, a unified benchmark designed to assess large language models' ability to perform comprehensive electroencephalography (EEG) analysis, including foundational analysis, sleep assessment, neurocognitive evaluation, and physiological integration. The benchmark covers 17 datasets and numerous tasks, requiring models to interpret EEG recordings and generate scientifically grounded reports evaluated through various output types. Testing across multiple models and execution methods revealed significant variability in performance, indicating that EEG understanding depends on both the model and its operational approach. BrainBench aims to provide a standardized platform to advance LLM-based EEG analysis tools, with code and results to be publicly released.

items.title: Researchers develop adversarially robust neurosymbolic fusion method for pre-trained transformer-based perception models using vector-space geometry without domain knowledge [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced a new method to enhance the robustness of pre-trained transformer-based perception models against distributional shifts in novel environments. Their approach replaces traditional majority voting with a metacognitive layer that learns error-detection rules from vector-space geometry derived from each model's training embeddings, avoiding reliance on hand-crafted domain knowledge. This neurosymbolic method frames the fusion of multiple imperfect vision transformer detectors as a consistency-based abduction problem solved via integer programming and heuristics. Evaluated on an aerial imagery benchmark with 15 weather-shifted test sets and six detectors, the method matches majority voting performance on clean data and significantly outperforms it under coordinated label-flipping attacks, maintaining higher F1 scores at high flip rates.

items.title: Researchers introduce the RAIL principles-Reasoning, Assurances, Interfacing, and Learning-as a framework for neurosymbolic AI to improve reliability and trustworthiness in AI systems [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A recent paper presents the RAIL principles as a unified framework for neurosymbolic AI, which integrates machine learning with symbolic reasoning to enhance AI performance in high-stakes and low-data environments. The authors argue that many existing AI systems, including those not traditionally classified as neurosymbolic, can be understood through this lens, offering a new perspective on AI design. The framework covers applications such as physics-aware machine learning, neuro-guided search like DeepMind's Alpha-* series, causal learning, and tool-augmented large language models. By applying the RAIL principles, engineers can make more informed decisions about designing and deploying trustworthy AI technologies across various domains.

items.title: Researchers develop NeuMoSync, a neuromodulatory neural network architecture enhancing plasticity and adaptability in continual learning across multiple benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have introduced NeuMoSync, a neural network architecture inspired by the brain's neuromodulatory systems, designed to improve continual learning by dynamically regulating neuron activation and synaptic plasticity. NeuMoSync incorporates neuron-specific modulation and a higher-level module that adapts based on current inputs and the network's state, aiming to address plasticity loss and poor knowledge transfer in sequential task learning. The architecture was evaluated on diverse continual learning benchmarks, including memorization, concept drift, class-incremental, and domain-incremental tasks, where it demonstrated improved adaptability and plasticity compared to existing methods. Ablation studies confirmed the importance of its components, and analysis revealed interpretable coordination patterns in the modulatory signals. The implementation code is publicly available on GitHub.

items.title: Researchers find that self-distillation with privileged information biases teachers and fails to improve model reasoning across complex tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers examined self-distillation (SD) methods where a teacher model, conditioned on privileged information like reference solutions, supervises a student model that lacks this information. While SD showed gains in simple tasks, the study found it does not improve performance on more difficult tasks such as question answering, mathematics, coding, and multi-turn tool use, with validation accuracy often degrading despite decreasing per-token loss. The failure is attributed to bias introduced by privileged information, which causes the teacher's targets to favor specific solution trajectories rather than general correctness. This bias leads the student model to focus on low-information tokens and penalize necessary reasoning hesitation, resulting in a less decisive model that does not improve reasoning ability. The findings suggest that as a standalone objective without reward signals, self-distillation optimizes a training signal disconnected from actual task success.

items.title: Researchers introduce WorldCycle, a self-verifiable reinforcement learning framework using reversible action cycles to improve long-horizon video world models and reduce state returning drift by up to 44% [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers present WorldCycle, a reinforcement learning framework designed to enhance interactive video world models for long-horizon planning by addressing compounding errors through self-verification using reversible action cycles. This approach constructs closed action cycles from ordinary sequences and optimizes spatial closure and temporal consistency rewards to enforce accurate state transitions without relying on ground-truth future states. The team also released CycleBench, a benchmark for evaluating state-returning ability under complex action structures, demonstrating that WorldCycle improves composite-action accuracy nearly fourfold compared to base models. This work provides a foundation for more physically grounded and reliable world models in video-based reinforcement learning.

items.title: Researchers report 41-day live challenge results for EU-AI Act compliant short-term load forecasting pipeline on German transmission-grid load [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: A 41-day live challenge evaluated a short-term load forecasting (STLF) pipeline designed to meet EU-AI Act requirements for safety-critical environments, focusing on the aggregated German transmission-grid load. The pipeline, based on the open-source Python library spotforecast2-safe, predicts 24 hourly load values using ENTSO-E data and incorporates anomaly detection, gap-aware data preparation, calendar and weather covariates, recursive multi-step forecasting, and hyperparameter tuning. It outperformed the official ENTSO-E day-ahead forecast baseline during the challenge. The study highlights that STLF is not only an accuracy challenge but also a software engineering and compliance issue due to legal requirements for determinism, reproducibility, and auditability in critical infrastructure. Transparent, low-cost, and auditable local models demonstrated competitive performance compared to large, energy-intensive pre-trained foundation models. The challenge infrastructure, submission history, and final leaderboard are publicly available for further analysis.

items.title: Researchers introduce OctoLong pipeline to enhance long-context language model training with cross-repository code contexts, improving code understanding and long-range retrieval [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed OctoLong, a context engineering pipeline that uses an AST parser, language server backend, and package manager to recursively retrieve code references, creating dependency-rich code contexts millions of tokens long. They trained OctoLong-Instruct, a suite of long-context open language models ranging from 600 million to 14 billion parameters, using a 50 billion token mixture including 6.2 billion tokens from OctoLong code contexts, followed by instruction tuning. Experimental evaluations against 18 state-of-the-art open-weight long-context language models show that replacing 12% of traditional context-extension corpora with OctoLong data significantly improves long-range retrieval, long-term state tracking, repository-level code understanding, and downstream agentic tasks, while also enhancing API usage in short-context coding scenarios.

items.title: C2MOE proposes a consistency and complementarity-guided mixture of experts framework for incomplete multimodal emotion recognition, improving robustness and imputation accuracy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers introduce C2MOE, a novel framework addressing missing modalities in multimodal emotion recognition by factorizing knowledge into consistency and complementarity components using interaction-aware experts. The approach combines representation learning and missing modality imputation through a dual-branch prediction mechanism that aligns imputed features with joint distributions and exploits modality-unique cues. C2MOE employs a learnable reweighting module to dynamically fuse expert outputs, enhancing robustness and adaptability. Experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that C2MOE outperforms state-of-the-art methods across various missing-modality scenarios, validating its effectiveness and generalization capabilities.

items.title: Researchers develop Hamming-Lipschitz stability theory for subdominant ultrametrics, showing sparse edits affect ultrametric entries only via minimum spanning tree paths [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: The subdominant (minmax) ultrametric, used as a tree-structured summary of dissimilarity matrices and induced by single-linkage clustering, has classical stability bounds that poorly handle sparse perturbations. Researchers developed an \(\ell_0\)-type stability theory demonstrating that changes in pairwise ultrametric values occur only if their tree path crosses an edited edge or a newly exposed cut from an off-tree edge, leading to precise bounds on the number of affected ultrametric entries. The analysis includes sharpness results proving that the dependence on tree geometry is unavoidable, with explicit examples where a single edited distance can change a quadratic number of ultrametric entries. A conditional near-additivity principle for multiple edits is also established. Experiments on deep-embedding graphs indicate that these structural scores can diagnose vulnerabilities in hierarchical representations.

items.title: Researchers develop AI-driven multimodal framework to uncover latent pathways linking socioeconomic disadvantage, psychosocial factors, and cardiometabolic multimorbidity using All of Us data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers created an AI-based multimodal mediation framework integrating socioeconomic, psychosocial, clinical, laboratory, behavioral, and genomic data from 20,804 participants in the All of Us Research Program to study links between social disadvantage and multimorbidity. They used variational autoencoders to derive latent representations of each data domain and performed mediation analyses to identify indirect associations among socioeconomic disadvantage, psychosocial vulnerability, and cardiometabolic multimorbidity. The strongest indirect association involved a latent socioeconomic disadvantage dimension, a psychosocial vulnerability dimension characterized by poorer mental health and social well-being, and a cardiometabolic multimorbidity dimension associated with conditions like hypertension, diabetes, and heart disease. Bootstrap analyses confirmed the stability of this pathway. The study demonstrates how AI representation learning can elucidate complex relationships across high-dimensional multimodal health data.

items.title: Researchers develop a trust-region framework for adaptive moment estimation in stochastic gradient optimization, introducing Gmake with moment constraints from order 2 to 4 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers propose a trust-region framework to analyze adaptive moment estimation methods like Adam in stochastic gradient optimization, constraining update steps by moment constraints of order p between 2 and 4. This framework leads to a family of learning-rate mechanisms based on second-moment and normalized p-th moment estimations, with p=4 involving kurtosis-like estimation, unified under the mechanism called Gmake. Experiments on GPT2-124M models trained on FineWeb-Edu and TinyStories datasets show that the fourth-moment approach benefits most when trust-region constraints are weak, while stronger constraints make the second-moment approach more competitive, often yielding slightly lower validation loss than the fourth-moment method.

items.title: Researchers introduce a Lindblad-inspired multi-timescale reservoir computing model with separable rotation and dissipation for improved temporal learning and stability [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers propose a new reservoir computing architecture inspired by Lindblad dynamics that separates reversible mixing and irreversible forgetting through independently tunable rotation and dissipation parameters. This design preserves stability without spectral-radius rescaling and allows explicit control over memory and mixing in echo-state networks. The model was evaluated against various reservoir types and a gated recurrent unit across multiple benchmarks, achieving top performance on tasks like bounded NARMA-20 and Lorenz-63 forecasting. Ablation studies highlight that rotation enhances state diversity while dissipation enables controlled forgetting and better predictive conditioning, offering an interpretable and stable recurrent framework.

items.title: Researchers fine-tune open-source diffusion models for nuclear energy text-to-image generation, improving accuracy over general-purpose and commercial AI systems [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers conducted a systematic study on adapting text-to-image AI models for nuclear engineering by fine-tuning three open-source diffusion models using a curated dataset of 1,000 captioned nuclear energy images. The fine-tuned models were evaluated quantitatively and qualitatively, showing substantial fidelity improvements for Stable Diffusion XL, limited gains for SD-v3.5-Medium, and no improvement for Flux.1, highlighting the importance of model architecture in adaptation effectiveness. The study also compared these fine-tuned models against leading commercial systems like GPT-Image-2, Gemini-3.1-Flash-Image, and Midjourney, finding that while commercial models generate convincing images for broad nuclear concepts, they often fail on specialized engineering prompts. The fine-tuned open-source models produced more accurate and technically consistent outputs, suggesting domain-specific fine-tuning as a viable approach for developing reliable generative AI tools in specialized fields.

items.title: Researchers evaluate robust and personalized federated learning methods for aircraft engine remaining-useful-life prediction under benign and adversarial client heterogeneity [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: This study investigates federated learning approaches that allow aircraft fleet operators to collaboratively train models predicting engine remaining useful life without sharing raw data. It addresses challenges from benign heterogeneity, where operators experience different conditions, and adversarial heterogeneity, where some submit poisoned updates. Using a multi-task convolutional neural network on a non-IID partition of the C-MAPSS benchmark, the researchers compare remedies for benign heterogeneity and test attacks against aggregation methods, including a sensor-value backdoor designed to mask engine degradation.

items.title: Researchers propose temporal QBER based machine learning framework to detect and classify stealthy eavesdropping attacks in BB84 quantum key distribution systems [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Conventional BB84 Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) systems use a fixed 11% Quantum Bit Error Rate (QBER) threshold to detect eavesdropping, but stealthy attacks can evade this detection. This study introduces a machine learning framework that analyzes 63 physics-informed temporal features of QBER to improve detection accuracy and classify multiple attack types under noisy and lossy conditions. The framework, tested with Random Forest, XGBoost, and SVM classifiers, significantly outperforms the traditional threshold method, reducing false negatives from 84.77% to 1.98% and achieving up to 88% accuracy with explainable feature importance.

items.title: Researchers introduce Recurrent Residual Quantization, a post-training method enabling multi-precision weight representations for large language models from a single checkpoint [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers propose Recurrent Residual Quantization (RRQ), a post-training quantization framework that represents large language model weights as a low-bit quantized base plus sequential quantized residuals, allowing multiple effective precisions from one checkpoint. Starting from a 2-bit model, RRQ progressively adds 2-bit residuals to build 4-, 6-, and 8-bit representations without requiring calibration or joint multi-bit optimization. In tests on six recent large language models, RRQ achieved competitive accuracy at 6 and 8 bits, with variable results at 4 bits, and constructed a full 2-/4-/6-/8-bit package 3.3 times faster than a comparable method in a Qwen3-8B setup. The code will be publicly released upon publication.

items.title: Researchers propose MACH, a hierarchical prototype hypergraph model capturing multimodal agreement and conflict for improved intent recognition [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers introduce MACH (Modality Agreement- and Conflict-aware prototype Hypergraph), a framework designed to enhance multimodal intent recognition by modeling both agreement and conflict among textual, acoustic, and visual signals. Unlike traditional methods that suppress modality inconsistencies, MACH represents these disagreements as distinct relational structures through hierarchical prototype hypergraphs, progressively composing unimodal to trimodal abstractions. MACH employs separate pathways for agreement and conflict, combined via a feature-wise, sample-adaptive arbitration mechanism to preserve informative disagreements while reducing noise. The model is optimized progressively to stabilize its hierarchical structure before joint learning. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate MACH's effectiveness, with analyses confirming the importance of its hierarchical composition, semantic refinement, and agreement-conflict arbitration components.

items.title: LaPrune introduces a differentiable layer for controllable sparsity with exact budget control and normalized second moment at million-scale models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: LaPrune is a new differentiable layer designed to control sparsity in large-scale models by preserving the selected mass and managing the normalized second moment. It uses a LapSum barrier and a normalized second-moment constraint to transition masks from dense equal-mass allocations toward hard top-k selections, enabling gradient flow where traditional hard selection blocks it. The method provides a population prediction of the saturated fraction, a near-binary limiting behavior, and a worst-case guarantee on the near-zero fraction. Its normalized hardness parameter remains invariant to score scale, addressing limitations of fixed LapSum temperature approaches.

items.title: Researchers introduce SJEPA, a hybrid symbolic-neural framework for learning compact latent dynamics with predictive representations and symbolic descriptions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers present SJEPA, a reconstruction-free joint-embedding predictive architecture that combines symbolic laws with neural corrections to learn predictive representations whose dynamics admit compact symbolic descriptions. The framework aims to balance predictive fidelity, representation quality, and symbolic parsimony by enforcing constraints that preserve informative predictive coordinates and favor low-complexity symbolic-neural transitions. In controlled pendulum experiments, SJEPA's joint learning approach discovers simpler symbolic dynamics with lower long-horizon rollout errors compared to post-hoc fitting, while regularization helps maintain symbolic mechanisms under grammar misspecification. The study formalizes induced-dynamics complexity and highlights trade-offs among predictive accuracy, representation collapse, and symbolic-neural allocation in latent dynamics modeling.

items.title: Researchers propose FBID, an adaptive personalized federated learning framework using server-side control to improve out-of-distribution attack detection in heterogeneous IoT networks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers introduce Federated Bandit Intrusion Detection (FBID), a personalized federated learning framework designed to enhance intrusion detection in heterogeneous IoT environments by addressing over-personalization issues in out-of-distribution (OOD) attack detection. FBID employs a contextual multi-armed bandit at the server to dynamically adjust each client's local training intensity and uses a trust-based blending mechanism to balance global and local model knowledge. Extensive experiments on the CICIoT2023 dataset under diverse client distributions and OOD stress-test conditions demonstrate that FBID improves individual client OOD detection rates by up to 7.66% and F1 scores by up to 5.08% relative to the strongest baseline, while also enhancing robustness against previously unseen attack classes.

items.title: Researchers propose NOVA-KV, a vector quantization method for KV cache in long-context LLM decoding that preserves attention accuracy at two bits per element [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers introduce NOVA-KV, a method that reduces key-value (KV) cache size in long-context large language model (LLM) decoding to improve throughput by preserving attention products with efficient vector quantization. The approach formulates KV cache quantization as a transform coding problem, deriving optimal non-orthogonal transforms from calibration statistics to minimize attention distortion while meeting fixed per-token bit constraints. NOVA-KV applies mean-squared error-optimal vector quantizers to transformed key coefficients and groups coefficients into equal-volume partitions to achieve variable-rate optimum with equal-size codebooks. At two bits per element, this method recovers most of the long-context retrieval accuracy lost by previous scalar quantization techniques without sacrificing throughput.

items.title: Researchers propose spatiotemporal graph Transformer for traffic forecasting in edge computing, outperforming recurrent graph models on real-world cellular data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers have developed a spatiotemporal graph Transformer framework to improve traffic forecasting in edge computing environments, where service demand changes dynamically across space and time. The model combines graph neural networks to capture spatial correlations among service regions with Transformer-based self-attention to learn long-range temporal dependencies, addressing limitations of existing recurrent forecasting methods in modeling long-term traffic evolution. Extensive experiments on a real-world cellular network dataset show that the proposed graph Transformer consistently outperforms recurrent graph-based baselines such as GCN-RNN, GCN-LSTM, and GCN-GRU across multiple forecasting horizons. The improved forecasts enable more effective proactive resource provisioning and reduce overload risks compared to reactive management strategies, highlighting the potential of graph-enhanced attention mechanisms for intelligent and adaptive edge computing systems.

items.title: Researchers propose Out-Of-The-Loop Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization using historical high-fidelity data and task descriptors to improve optimization when highest-fidelity queries are too costly [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization (MF-BO) typically leverages correlations across different fidelity levels to optimize expensive black-box functions. However, in many real-world scenarios, querying the highest-fidelity function is prohibitively expensive, though practitioners often have access to historical high-fidelity data from previous experiments. This work identifies the suboptimality of standard MF-BO algorithms under these conditions and introduces a method that incorporates historical high-fidelity observations along with task descriptors, which can be explicit or extracted from metadata, to enhance optimization performance. The proposed approach is validated on synthetic benchmarks and real-world applications including molecular optimization and hyperparameter tuning. By integrating prior high-fidelity data outside the optimization loop, the method addresses practical challenges where the true objective function cannot be frequently evaluated, demonstrating improved effectiveness over traditional MF-BO techniques.

items.title: InvFlowFD introduces a reference-free, background-set-free music quality metric using Flow Matching inversion to detect distortions and rank generative models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers propose InvFlowFD, a novel music perceptual quality metric that eliminates the need for paired noisy-clean data and background sets by leveraging a pre-trained Flow Matching backbone. This method uses unconditional Flow Matching inversion via Euler integration to identify artificial distortions and align model rankings with human perceptual judgments. Evaluations against prior metrics and a comprehensive human study show that InvFlowFD correlates strongly with human perception while offering greater flexibility and fewer restrictions than existing approaches.

items.title: Researchers introduce LiNC, a lightweight noise correction method using per-sample trust parameters and Gaussian Mixture Modeling to improve label noise handling in medical imaging datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Label noise in medical imaging datasets, caused by factors like inter-rater variability and annotation errors, can reduce the reliability of machine learning models. To address this, researchers developed Lightweight Noise Correction (LiNC), which assigns a trainable trust parameter to each training sample to balance reliance on observed labels versus model predictions during training. LiNC uses a Gaussian Mixture Model to classify samples as clean, ambiguous, or noisy and applies correction phases accordingly, improving accuracy and mislabel detection on ten 2D MedMNISTv2 datasets with up to 50% label noise. LiNC maintains training efficiency with negligible overhead, as its complexity remains dominated by the base network and memory usage grows linearly with the training set size. This approach offers a practical solution for enhancing model robustness against label noise in clinical imaging applications.

items.title: Researchers introduce Trident, an agentic LLM framework that breaks deep reinforcement learning cyber defenses by reducing blue agent performance by 522% using adaptive attack strategies [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.content_text: Researchers present Trident, a new agentic large language model (LLM) red teaming framework designed to evaluate and challenge autonomous cyber defense systems based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL). Trident includes a dynamic benchmark environment, a dataset of over 13,000 red-blue interaction trajectories, and a novel "Code-as-Policy" architecture that trains adaptive red agents to generate and execute attack strategies against DRL defenders. The framework's trainable planner autonomously discovers sophisticated attack behaviors such as decoy avoidance and adaptive state prioritization, which static heuristic red agents fail to uncover. Empirical tests show that Trident significantly degrades the defensive performance of existing DRL-based cyber defense agents, revealing fundamental vulnerabilities in current autonomous defense approaches.

items.title: Researchers propose Lexi-LowGLM, an efficient online algorithm for generalized low-rank matrix bandits with multiple prioritized objectives using lexicographic preference order [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: This paper introduces Lexi-LowGLM, an online algorithm designed for generalized low-rank matrix bandits where multiple objectives have different priority levels evaluated lexicographically. The method estimates objective-specific low-rank subspaces and updates estimators via an online Newton step, reducing update complexity from quadratic to linear over time. The authors establish a regret bound dependent on the effective low-rank dimension rather than the ambient dimension, and numerical experiments demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness and computational efficiency.

items.title: Researchers introduce ATLAS, a reinforcement learning method using adaptive topological learning and abstract successors to improve sample efficiency and adaptability in non-stationary environments [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: ATLAS combines a Grow When Required network with Successor Features to address low sample efficiency and catastrophic forgetting in reinforcement learning. Evaluated on spatial navigation tasks, it structurally decouples transition dynamics from reward signals, enabling near-instantaneous adaptation to new goals and positive backward transfer. The method significantly outperforms common on-policy and off-policy algorithms in environments with shifting conditions.

items.title: Researchers introduce iStructTab with Graph-Enhanced Descriptor Sequencing to improve multimodal learning of image and tabular data by reducing feature dispersion [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers present iStructTab, a multimodal learning approach that combines images and tabular data using Graph-Enhanced Descriptor Sequencing (GEDS), an algorithm based on the Column Permutation Problem to optimize feature sequencing. The method integrates GEDS within an order-aware transformer framework that enforces feature order through memory tokens and a dedicated loss function. Experimental results on multimodal benchmarks show that iStructTab reduces feature redundancy and dispersion, enhancing predictive performance and robustness, highlighting the importance of structured feature sequencing in multimodal learning.

items.title: Researchers propose HyperTrust framework to improve hypergraph neural network robustness against label noise with trustworthiness estimation and structure adjustment [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers present a systematic study on hypergraph node classification under label noise, adapting existing learning methods and revealing their limitations. They propose HyperTrust, a framework that estimates hyperedge trustworthiness and uses modules to enhance reliable supervision and suppress noise, improving prediction accuracy. HyperTrust combines a pretraining-based, entropy-aware strategy with HyperedgeBoost and HyperedgePrune modules to connect unlabeled nodes to trustworthy hyperedges and remove noisy connections. Experiments and theoretical analysis demonstrate its effectiveness across multiple hypergraph datasets and noisy conditions, providing a unified benchmark and foundation for future research in hypergraph learning with label noise.

items.title: NodeJEPA introduces structure-conditioned latent prediction for node-level graph self-supervised learning without input reconstruction or handcrafted augmentations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: NodeJEPA is a joint-embedding predictive architecture designed for node-level graph self-supervised learning that predicts latent representations of masked k-hop ego-subgraphs using a context encoder and a target encoder updated via exponential moving average. The model incorporates a structure-conditioned predictor that uses spectral and centrality descriptors through cross-attention, along with variance, covariance, and Laplacian spectral regularizers to stabilize embedding geometry, and optionally employs a curriculum to increase masking difficulty during training. Evaluated on standard node classification benchmarks with linear probing and fine-tuning, NodeJEPA offers a practical approach to node-level JEPA-style latent prediction and clarifies the benefits of structural conditioning in representation learning; its code and evaluation scripts are publicly available.

items.title: BinaryPC introduces training-free, data-aware hashing-based sparse attention for long-context large language models, improving decoding throughput by 3.56× over FlashAttention [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers present BinaryPC, a new sparse attention method for long-context large language models that uses binary principal components to create compact binary hash codes without requiring training. This approach preserves structural data information better than existing methods like Locality-Sensitive Hashing and avoids accuracy degradation common in sparse attention techniques. Experiments across multiple model families and benchmarks show that BinaryPC maintains accuracy comparable to full attention while outperforming other sparse and hashing-based baselines. On modern GPUs, BinaryPC achieves a 3.56× speedup in end-to-end decoding throughput compared to the FlashAttention kernel.

items.title: Researchers propose MESH, a memory-efficient Sinkhorn optimization method for Mixture-of-Experts training that reduces optimizer state memory by 62.5% while maintaining performance [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers identified that direct application of Sinkhorn gradient descent to Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) training is unreliable due to conditional and temporally varying gradients in expert matrices. They developed MESH, a hidden-momentum Sinkhorn update that restores temporal smoothing without storing full optimizer state, reducing memory usage significantly compared to AdamW. In experiments with a 110M-parameter MoE model, MESH and its block-preconditioned variant cut optimizer-state memory by 62.5% and peak CUDA allocation by about 12.6%, with only a modest evaluation loss increase. Ablation studies confirmed that temporal smoothing before matrix normalization is critical for MoE expert optimization, while full coordinate-wise AdamW state is not necessary.

items.title: Researchers propose counterfactual recoverability to guide selective supervision in on-policy distillation, improving performance on AIME benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers introduce counterfactual recoverability as a method to determine whether errors in on-policy distillation (OPD) can be corrected, using teacher-continuation and rollback branches to classify states as recoverable, irreversible-but-avoidable, or ambiguous. This approach guides training decisions to retain, roll back, or conventionally supervise trajectories, outperforming divergence-based rules. Evaluations on AIME benchmarks show that recoverability-aware control achieves higher success rates than baselines, with a recoverability proxy reaching an AUC of 1.000 compared to 0.392 for divergence alone. Component analysis indicates that retaining teacher-correctable prefixes contributes most to performance gains, establishing recoverability as a key decision variable for selective supervision in OPD.

items.title: Researchers introduce SPOT, a method for on-policy distillation that uses sparse probing and outcome calibration to improve reasoning performance across multiple student models and benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers present SPOT (Sparse Probing and Outcome-calibrated Targets), a new approach to on-policy distillation that addresses where to probe and what to distill by combining teacher entropy, candidate probability mass, and student-teacher mismatch. SPOT evaluates teacher-proposed candidates through verifier-scored student continuations and produces a KL-regularized target favoring candidates with better downstream outcomes while staying anchored to the teacher distribution. Extensive experiments demonstrate SPOT's effectiveness in enhancing reasoning performance while balancing solution quality and coverage across various student models and reasoning benchmarks.

items.title: Researchers propose GOAL, a generative framework for optimizing incentivized advertising under global constraints using hierarchical causal state encoding and safe constrained policy optimization [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers introduce GOAL, a constraint-aware generative framework that optimizes continuous incentive magnitudes in incentivized advertising by modeling incentive allocation as a conditional sequence generation problem. GOAL incorporates a hierarchical causal state encoder to capture user behavior dynamics and system-level constraints, addressing challenges like high-frequency interactions, delayed feedback, and user fatigue that limit existing methods. The framework includes Safe Constrained Policy Optimization (SCPO), which learns a single generative policy adaptable across various ROI constraints without retraining. Experiments on large-scale real-world data and synthetic environments demonstrate that GOAL improves long-term revenue and user retention while significantly reducing ROI violations compared to strong baseline approaches.

items.title: Researchers propose a tropical algebraic geometry-based descriptor using Arakelov-Green measure for graph learning to improve 3D neuronal morphology analysis beyond 1-WL limitations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers introduce a training-free geometric prior based on tropical algebraic geometry to enhance the analysis of 3D neuronal morphologies by capturing both graph topology and spatial geometry. Their method transforms spatial trees into cyclic metric graphs embedded into the Tropical Jacobian, using the Arakelov-Green measure computed via the graph Laplacian's generalized inverse to avoid NP-hard lattice searches. This approach yields node-level structural coordinates and a graph-level signature that surpass the expressivity limits of current message-passing Graph Neural Networks bounded by the 1-Weisfeiler-Lehman test. The proposed descriptors integrate seamlessly into standard architectures such as VAEs, GNNs, and Tree-LSTMs without additional trainable parameters. Evaluations on benchmarks including BREC and 3D morphology datasets (ACT-4, JML-4, BIL-6) demonstrate improved classification accuracy and performance over existing spatial models and explicit lattice approximations, highlighting the method's potential for advancing graph learning in neuronal data analysis.

items.title: Researchers propose Neural Bilinear Dynamical Model for nonlinear time series forecasting, integrating control inputs and error compensation for improved long-horizon predictions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers introduce the Neural Bilinear Dynamical Model (NBDM) to improve forecasting of nonlinear time series generated by complex dynamical systems. NBDM uses Koopman theory to lift nonlinear dynamics into a higher-dimensional latent space and models state evolution with a bilinear dynamical system, incorporating a parameterized error compensation term to reduce approximation errors. The model explicitly integrates control inputs and employs a memory-enhanced controller to infer missing controls through interactions between historical states and control signals. Experiments on five real-world datasets show that NBDM outperforms existing methods in both given-control and missing-control scenarios, especially for multi-step and long-horizon forecasting tasks.

items.title: Researchers propose MCU, a model merging approach for continual unlearning in multimodal large language models to address cumulative utility degradation and retention drift [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Researchers introduce Merging for Continual Unlearning (MCU), a method that dynamically merges multiple one-shot unlearning adapters into a unified adapter to handle continual unlearning requests in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). This approach aims to overcome issues in existing methods, such as cumulative utility degradation, unlearning rebound, and retention drift caused by repeated one-shot unlearning operations. MCU uses a leave-one-out merging analysis to reveal strong cross-task dependencies among unlearning adapters, which can both facilitate transferability and cause interference that reduces unlearning effectiveness. To mitigate this, MCU projects adapters into a shared representation space, preserves dominant directions, suppresses over-concentrated coordinates, and reconfigures dependencies to enhance transferability while reducing interference. Experiments on ICU-Bench and MLLMU-Bench show that MCU improves unlearning effectiveness while maintaining retained knowledge and overall multimodal utility.

items.title: Researchers find frontier language models solve only 56.9% of European executive decision tasks compared to near-ceiling expert performance [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A study evaluated six leading large language models (LLMs) on EuroExec, a benchmark of 413 open-ended European executive tasks created by 47 domain experts. Over 4,000 human expert hours were spent manually assessing model responses using detailed rubrics and preference rankings, revealing that the best model solved just 56.9% of tasks while expert-written answers were preferred in 74% of comparisons. The research highlights that current frontier LLMs fall significantly short of professional expert standards on complex, real-world decision-making problems and that human evaluation remains essential for accurate assessment.

items.title: Researchers propose Dynamical Mode Pruning to improve Echo State Networks by ranking neurons based on dynamic influence rather than static metrics [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Researchers propose Dynamical Mode Pruning (DMP), a method to prune Echo State Networks (ESNs) by evaluating neurons' contributions to dominant transition modes derived from a trajectory-averaged Jacobian Gramian. This approach targets dynamically redundant neurons often overlooked by static pruning methods. Experiments on chaotic and real-world time-series data show that DMP maintains or improves forecasting accuracy while reducing reservoir size by removing low-impact units and retraining only the readout layer. The findings suggest that considering dynamical influence offers a more effective criterion for refining ESN reservoirs than static connectivity or activation statistics alone.

items.title: Personalized Federated Sparse Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2608.04695v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated adaptation of time-series foundation models (TSFMs) is attractive for building energy forecasting because meter data are private, distributed, and highly non-IID. However, a single parameter-sharing strategy is unlikely to serve all pretrained TSFMs or building clients: fully shared adapters can suppress building-specific temporal behavior, while fully local adaptation discards cross-building transfer. We propose a personalized federated sparse adaptation framework with a heterogeneous temporal mixture-of-experts (MoE) adapter placed after the pretrained TSFM representation. A sequence-level router maps each 168-hour context window to a top-$k$ subset of experts specialized for periodicity, long-range interactions, local variation, trend-residual structure, and multi-resolution behavior. We compare global FL, local training, and personalized FL variants with globally shared or client-private expert banks. Across 50 buildings and three TSFM backbones, personalization consistently outperforms Global FL-MoE and Local MoE, while the best sparse-adaptation strategy varies by backbone and metric. Routing behavior further reveals client-level expert specialization, expert concentration, and near-uniform routing across backbones, showing that federated TSFM adaptation should be both client-aware and backbone-aware.

items.title: Design Choices That Matter: A Functional ANOVA Analysis for Remote Sensing Multi-Label Classification [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2608.04702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Benchmarking deep learning (DL) models for multi-label classification (MLC) of remote sensing images (RSI) typically yields rankings that do not generalize beyond the evaluated datasets. In this work, we move beyond rankings by employing functional analysis of variance (fANOVA) to systematically quantify the contributions of individual design choices and their interactions to performance variability. We conduct two empirical analyses covering 48 and 20 DL models, respectively, spanning design choices such as network architecture, fine-tuning strategy, learning strategy, and initialization. By applying fANOVA across seven MLC RSI datasets, we construct dataset meta-representations that capture design-choice sensitivity profiles. Hierarchical clustering of these meta-representations reveals that datasets naturally group according to how they respond to design decisions, with patterns strongly linked to intrinsic dataset properties such as scale, spatial resolution, and label space complexity. Our findings show that for large-scale datasets, fine-tuning strategy and architecture are dominant factors, while in data-limited regimes, initialization becomes decisive. For intermediate regimes, the interaction between architecture and learning strategy governs performance.

items.title: A 6G Integrated Sensing and Communication Framework for Railway Intrusion Detection and Collision Prediction [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2608.04710v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) combines sensing and communication to efficiently utilize wireless resources and is emerging as a key paradigm for next-generation wireless networks. By leveraging the wide bandwidth, high frequencies, and massive antenna arrays of 5G-Advanced and 6G systems, ISAC enables physical-layer sensing using Channel State Information (CSI). The 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) Release 19 identifies 32 potential ISAC use cases, with particular emphasis on detecting and tracking moving objects. In this work, we address the Sensing for Railway Intrusion Detection use case, where intruders, including wildlife, entering a railway track can pose serious collision risks. We generated 22,695 CSI matrices with corresponding ground truth using a 3D-rendered railway environment and the Sionna radio simulator. We developed a machine learning model combining a three-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (3D CNN) and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network to detect intruders in the track danger zone and estimate their real-time position relative to the train, velocity, and time to collision. On synthetic CSI data, the model achieves 99.57% intruder-detection accuracy on a balanced test set and a combined Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.4240 for position, velocity, and time-to-collision prediction. These results demonstrate the potential of CSI-based ISAC sensing with machine learning for reliable railway intrusion detection. The complete codebase for CSI generation, preprocessing, and model development is publicly available at https://github.com/EdgeIntelligenceLab/6g-isac-railway-intrusion-detection.

items.title: What We Observe as LLM Behavior Can Be a Side-effect of Inference Backend [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2608.04714v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Benchmark scores are reported as properties of a model, yet the inference framework used to produce them, such as HuggingFace, vLLM, or Ollama, are considered non-influential and their names and versions are almost never disclosed. In this work we investigate how much this choice can influence the model output. In a fully-crossed study (three instruction-tuned models x five inference frameworks x six benchmarks x four generation modes) we investigate how different tools (wrappers/backend) influence benchmark scores and how their score changes is influenced by generation hyper-parameters. We find backend to be a non-negligible factor where even under greedy, sampling-noise-free decoding, changing the backend can significantly alter models performance and this effect is structural and strongly model-dependent. Decomposing the variance according to generation mode reveal that considerable portion of the variability (roughly 39\%) a practitioner sees out-of-the-box can stem from the backend, while the remaining stems from sampling noise and each framework's default generation parameters, both of which are avoidable by disclosing and matching the generation configuration. These divergences are more pronounced on factual than on social-bias benchmarks. Overall, benchmark numbers are not backend-agnostic therefore, we recommend disclosing the backend, its version, and the full generation configuration, also using deterministic decoding for cross-backend comparison.

items.title: IMFACT: Counterfactual Explanations for Time Series via Intrinsic Mode Function Substitution [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2608.04777v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Oscillatory signals, such as vibration, carry class-discriminative information in specific frequency bands; perturbing them in raw feature space for counterfactual analysis easily destroys their temporal structure and produces physically implausible results. In this work, we introduce IMFACT (IMF-based counterfACTuals), a model-agnostic framework for generating plausible counterfactual explanations for time series classifiers that operates in the decomposition space of Empirical Mode Decomposition. An input signal is split into Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs), and selected IMFs are progressively substituted with those of a Nearest Unlike Neighbour (NUN) until the classifier flips to the target class. We evaluate six IMF-selection strategies and a multi-NUN cycling extension on two UCR benchmarks (FaultDetectionA, FruitFlies). The variance-based strategy with three NUNs outperforms two prominent baseline techniques on reliability and plausibility metrics, while cycling across three NUNs yields the best proximity across both datasets.

items.title: Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Observation-Calibrated Self-Distillation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2608.04788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model agents are commonly trained through reinforcement learning with sparse trajectory-level rewards, which offer limited guidance on how strongly individual tokens should be updated. On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) addresses this by re-scoring generated tokens under a privileged replay view to obtain dense, token-level supervision. However, we identify a confounding issue: the resulting support may reflect both the privileged information contained in the replay view and score shifts induced by the replay scaffold, making it difficult to attribute the support specifically to that information. This issue is especially pronounced when future environment observations serve as privileged information, since replaying them requires reconstructing an extended scaffold that itself perturbs token scores. To resolve this confounding, we propose Observation-Calibrated Self-Distillation (OCSD), which contrasts two structurally matched replay views, Full and Observation-Ablated, differing only in whether the actual future observation is present, to derive an observation residual that discounts score changes shared by the replay scaffold. OCSD then applies this residual to modulate token-level GRPO updates at high-uncertainty steps, while preserving the trajectory-level update direction. Experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, and Search-QA across three Qwen3 model scales show that OCSD consistently outperforms strong baselines. Diagnostic analyses further confirm that the calibrated residual aligns better with local environment feedback. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/yiy1x/OCSD.

items.title: A-SR: Self-Evolving Agentic LLMs for Symbolic Regression via Hierarchical Coordination [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2608.04872v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Symbolic regression aims to discover closed-form equations from data, but existing LLM-guided methods often rely on a unified proposal loop that compresses heterogeneous search failures into a scalar score and a single prompt. We propose A-SR, a self-evolving agentic framework that shifts the control unit from expression edits to role-conditioned evidence views. A-SR coordinates formula discovery through routing among coordination protocols, an online evaluator-reward role policy, and state-routed process memory. During search, evaluator feedback characterizes reliability and productivity, updates role-level utilities, and routes elite motifs, failure traces, and validity diagnostics to different agents. The framework self-evolves at two timescales: within a run, it adapts the search process without updating LLM parameters; across runs, recorded trajectories can be distilled into open-source LLMs as role-conditioned proposal priors. Averaged over the four LSR-Synth scientific domains in LLM-SRBench, A-SR improves Acc@0.01 over baselines from 25.79% to 48.30% with Llama3.1-8B, while A-SR-LoRA improves the corresponding Qwen3-4B result from 24.58% to 38.29%. On four real-world scientific discovery tasks, A-SR obtains the best in-distribution or out-of-distribution normalized mean squared error on 7 of 8 reported metrics.

items.title: When Does Latent Communication Pay? A Causal Audit of Relayed KV Caches in Multi-Agent LLMs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2608.04893v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems relay key--value caches instead of text and credit their gains to exchanged ``latent thoughts''. That credit is a claim about \emph{which} example's cache is relayed, not merely that one is. We audit it causally in released systems. The cache is replaced with deranged (mismatched-example), zeroed, and moment-matched random counterparts, under two regimes defined by whether the receiver needs the sender's private information. Where it does, the battery reads ceiling: 100\% against 23--25\% for answer-irrelevant relays on the primary backbone, a contrast replicated across three families, five checkpoints, and a prose document-QA surface. Where it does not, a pre-registered five-seed protocol establishes equivalence within 2.8 points, a margin anchored to the audited system's reported gain, under Holm-corrected TOST on GSM8K and ARC-Challenge across three Qwen3 scales and on MedQA at 8B (one cell shows a small detected advantage inside the margin); a second family shows no detected advantage. A large cache effect need not be a pairing effect. In one natural cell, zeroing the relay costs 14.7 points; a mismatched cache, 0.4. Nor is need sufficient: under the same test, delivered channels span ceiling (LatentMAS's native relay), partial (KVComm's layer subset), and no detected example-specific transfer (C2C's released projector). Benchmark deltas do not by themselves establish latent-thought transmission; establishing it takes a mismatched-cache audit, which we release.

items.title: Consistency-Driven Co-Evolution for Self-Supervised Cross-Representation Learning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2608.04926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As chart images, tabular data, and visualization code play increasingly important roles across diverse domains, cross-representation understanding across these modalities poses fundamental challenges for AI systems: the relationships across representations are inherently \textit{one-to-many}, supervision is ambiguous and costly, and model optimization lacks a principled signal that is both direction-adaptive and representation-generalizable beyond task-specific objectives. We introduce CoCoEvolve to improve consistency across chart, table, and code representations. Instead of treating cross-representation mapping as a one-to-many problem, we define explicit one-to-one correspondences and optimize models using agreement between representations, without additional annotations. During training, CoCoEvolve@Train performs co-evolution across the chart-table-code cycle, while CoCoEvolve@Test applies the same consistency objective at inference time for test-time co-optimization. We also present CoCoEvolve@Eval, an evaluation suite covering all six cross-representation tasks. Across four benchmarks, CoCoEvolve improves performance in both training-time and test-time settings. Our project page: https://xhguo7.github.io/CoCoEvolve/.

items.title: SVI-DAG: A Structured Variational Inference Approach to Bayesian Causal Discovery [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2608.04930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bayesian causal discovery seeks to determine the posterior distribution of causal theories, which are interpreted as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) that explain the observed data. The resulting posterior allows systematic reasoning regarding epistemic uncertainty within these theories. Nonetheless, finding such graphs is difficult due to identifiability problems and limited observational data. Furthermore, precisely approximating posterior over graphs is challenging given vast range of potential DAGs. Recent Bayesian approaches have addressed some of these challenges, yet they remain limited as they fail to encode dependencies between edges, and lack principled ways to incorporate domain knowledge as inductive biases during the search process. To overcome these limitations, we propose SVI-DAG, a structured variational inference approach to Bayesian causal discovery using observational data and prior beliefs that uses normalizing flows to model dependencies between edges, supporting expressive and multimodal posterior learning over DAGs. To mitigate mode seeking behaviour in evidence lower bound optimization and promote mode coverage, we use stein variational gradient descent to update the node potentials using a kernel in acyclicity space. We evaluate SVI-DAG against 5 state-of-the-art Bayesian DAG learning methods and demonstrate superior performance in uncertainty quantification while remaining competitive in terms of structural accuracy.

items.title: CheMLFlow: An Open-Source Platform for Cheminformatics and Materials Informatics Applications [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2608.04942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: CheMLFlow is an open-source platform for building and executing end-to-end, high-throughput, and agentic workflows for scientific and technological applications. CheMLFlow targets a common bottleneck in scientific machine learning development, where researchers often need to assemble data acquisition, curation, representation, model training, validation, screening, interpretation, and reporting into a reproducible pipeline, even when their primary research contribution concerns only one stage. CheMLFlow provides modular workflow components, ready-to-run reference pipelines, standardized artifacts, and evaluation outputs that reduce orchestration overhead and support benchmarking across methods and datasets. The platform is designed to be extensible, reproducible, and automation friendly, with pluggable representations and models, deterministic splits, explicit run artifacts, batch execution, and report generation. As scientific software increasingly moves toward agent assisted experimentation, CheMLFlow's configuration driven workflows and structured outputs also provide a practical interface for coding agents to help users construct experiments, inspect results, and summarize findings under human supervision. This article describes the system architecture, core workflows, and benchmarks that reach literature performance for quantum mechanical, physicochemical and bioactivity property prediction, and use cases involving time series datasets demonstrating applications beyond molecular chemistry datasets.

items.title: Protoreasoning in Tiny Transformers [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2608.04980v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that tiny transformers can profitably employ a simple form of Chain of Thought, which we call protoreasoning, allowing us to study step-by-step reasoning on ~1M-parameter models and opening up opportunities for much more detailed experimentation and analysis than is feasible for larger models. Current Large Language Models exhibit impressive step-by-step reasoning, but we have yet to understand its generality, i.e., when and how LLMs learn genuinely general algorithms rather than "bags of heuristics." Such questions are hard to settle on compute-intensive frontier models trained on opaque data. To work at model scales far below the threshold for natural-language competence, we define reasoning-friendly tasks on Dyck languages (sentences of correctly nested brackets). We find that protoreasoning traces substantially close the out-of-distribution generalization gap, and ablations confirm that the trace's content, not merely its extra tokens, drives the gain.

items.title: OneDayAgent: Towards a Long-Horizon Harness for Autonomous Agents [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2608.05013v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents are increasingly applied to open-ended everyday requests that span work, study, and life. These tasks are long-horizon, cross-environment, and multimodal, forcing the agent to preserve goals and constraints across many steps while navigating heterogeneous tools and attachments. While prior work has addressed individual failure modes such as goals drift, states loss, and context overflow, whether a single harness can manage them jointly and remain effective across backends has received less study. We present OneDayAgent, a long-horizon harness for autonomous agents. OneDayAgent turns an open-ended request into a managed execution process that decomposes tasks into bounded subtasks, maintains execution memory under context pressure, and verifies and repairs the final deliverable. We evaluate OneDayAgent on AgentIF-OneDay across 104 tasks. With the GLM-5.2 backend, OneDayAgent sets a new state of the art with an overall score of 0.821. The same harness runs across five backend LLMs from three model families, indicating the harness generalizes across backends without tuning, even as different models induce distinct execution styles under the same workflow.

items.title: Revealed Rationality: Label-Free Evaluation and Regularization from Representation Theorems [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2608.05015v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Representation theorems in decision theory establish that behavior satisfies certain axioms if and only if it can be rationalized by a well-defined objective. I argue that this ``if and only if'' structure provides a potentially useful foundation for label-free evaluation and regularization of LLMs and other AI systems. Axiom compliance can be checked from the model's own responses to synthetic choice problems, with no external labels or human feedback, and the penalties are readily computable. Because the axioms are necessary and sufficient, the resulting checks exhaust the implications of the relevant rationality standard for the elicited data: a model that passes cannot be rejected on rationality grounds by any further test of the same data. I discuss three instantiations: probabilistic coherence via a theorem of de Finetti, preference rationality via Afriat's theorem, and subjective expected utility via a theorem of Echenique and Saito (2015), each yielding a continuous penalty that is zero whenever behavior can be rationalized. Since coherence does not restrict which objective rationalizes behavior, these penalties complement rather than replace other evaluation and training signals.

items.title: MarsCast: Transfer Learning of AI Weather Foundation Models to Planetary Atmospheres [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2608.05054v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the transferability of Earth weather foundation models to planetary atmospheres by adapting the GraphCast graph neural weather forecasting model to Mars. While GraphCast achieves state-of-the-art performance for terrestrial forecasting, its applicability to non-Earth environments remains unexplored. Using the Mars Climate Database (MCD), which provides global atmospheric fields across vertical altitude levels (similar to Earth pressure levels), we evaluate zero-shot and fine-tuned GraphCast predictions of Martian temperature and wind fields. Zero-shot forecasts produce a surprisingly accurate depiction of current conditions but fail to reproduce diurnal variability and rapidly decay toward climatological mean states. To address this limitation, we fine-tune GraphCast using MCD variables and top-of-atmosphere solar radiation forcing while holding humidity constant. Fine-tuning enables rapid learning of Martian thermal variability. Within as few as 10 training epochs, the model begins to capture the diurnal cycle and forecasts up to 10 days reproduce seasonal and vertical temperature structure. Prediction quality improves with training sample size and exhibits sensitivity to seasonal initialization. These results demonstrate that Earth-trained AI weather models can be adapted to simulate Martian atmospheric dynamics, providing a pathway toward rapid planetary weather prediction to support mission operations, dust storm risk mitigation, and future human exploration.

items.title: Provable Limits and Certified Deferral for Verbalized Uncertainty in Small Language Models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2608.05064v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Small open-weight language models increasingly run in private, offline, and cost-sensitive settings, where the key deployment question is not only what a model answers but when it should defer to a human. We study whether verbalized confidence can support risk-controlled deferral, evaluating eleven instruction-tuned models from three families, 0.5B to 14B parameters, on ARC-Challenge and TruthfulQA with 25,168 local predictions. Three theoretical results delimit what calibration can provide: strictly monotone calibration preserves the risk-coverage frontier and error-detection AUROC; temperature scaling cannot calibrate models whose confidence stays above one half while accuracy falls below it; and a Clopper-Pearson procedure converts a 200-question calibration set into a finite-sample risk certificate under an i.i.d. deployment assumption. Empirically, eight of 22 model-task pairs hit the temperature-scaling infeasibility floor within one percentage point of the predicted bound. Platt scaling reduces ECE to as low as 0.02, yet certified autonomy at a 20% risk budget is granted to only three model-task pairs and to none at 10%. We also identify and repair an answer-ordering artifact in the multiple-choice form of TruthfulQA. Calibration gives confidence semantics; certified deferral determines when small models are safe to use.

items.title: MultiPathFormer: Towards a Foundation Model for Multipath Wireless Propagation [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2608.05076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in machine learning have enabled training of wireless foundation models, which aim to support tasks such as channel estimation, beam prediction, and localization based on wireless signals. Existing wireless foundation models typically pretrain on channel tensors using masked reconstruction over subcarriers, antennas, or time but ignore the physical characteristics of wireless propagation. In this work, we propose to instead use multipath propagation as the fundamental pretraining object. We present MultiPathFormer, an autoregressive foundation model that represents each transmitter-receiver link as an ordered sequence of continuous-valued path tokens and pretrains with next-path prediction. We introduce an Environmental RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) mechanism and a first-path codebook on top of the transformer backbone, leveraging environment knowledge to improve path statistics estimation like delay and power by up to 59%. MultiPathFormer pretrained on 27 environments transfers to unseen users and, after scenario-specific fine-tuning, outperforms training the corresponding models from scratch in new environments. Across downstream tasks, it outperforms SOTA channel-based foundation models, achieving 5.57 m mean localization error, 0.914 top-3 beam accuracy, 0.994 line-of-sight classification accuracy, and 0.561 channel estimation NMSE. These results show that path-level pretraining can learn reusable representations of wireless propagation.

items.title: Capability-Gated Planning: Cost-to-Goal Discovery and the Limits of Myopic Experiment Selection [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: arXiv:2608.05085v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Systems that automate scientific discovery must repeatedly decide which experiment to run, which hypothesis to test, which tool to build, and when to stop. Many systems make these decisions by maximizing a myopic score such as expected information gain per unit cost or a learned plausibility score. We identify a structural limitation of this approach. Some actions are constructive: they acquire an epistemic capability (an instrument, assay, pipeline, simulator, or abstraction) whose value lies not in the information returned immediately but in the future actions it makes available. When the least-cost route to a confident answer requires a chain of such constructions, a planner that scores actions only by information obtainable within a bounded horizon cannot value the first construction: it yields no information within the horizon and is dominated by any measurement with positive information, however small. We formulate goal-directed discovery as a stochastic shortest-path problem in belief space in which constructive experiments change the downstream action graph, and prove that for every lookahead depth d there is an instance on which every myopic information-maximizing planner has an unbounded approximation ratio, and a related instance on which it never reaches the goal. The mechanism is a capability-indistinguishability lemma: within the horizon, acquiring a capability can be observationally indistinguishable from paying for a null action. This establishes capability gating as a reachability axis of difficulty distinct from curvature (submodularity) and information order (adaptivity gaps). We introduce CG-Plan, an incremental replanner with a capability-aware cost-to-go heuristic h = h_cap + h_exp.
